title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 85 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 480–482 (Night 85, continuing directly from nights-84), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 85 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The old woman, having sent the king a sweetmeat from the supposed Men of the Unseen, wins his trust still further, and asks to take the five slave-girls to those hidden saints for their blessing, to be brought back rich on the last night of his fast. She also asks him to send one more person dear to him; he offers Ṣafiyya, a Rūmī slave-girl who bore him two children now lost, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifth and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-fifth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ النَّهَارُ صَامَ السُّلْطَانُ وَخَرَجَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-nahāru ṣāma al-sulṭānu wa-kharajati al-ʿajūzu ilā ḥāli sabīlihā
sentences.l: And when it was the day, the sultan fasted, and the old-woman went out to the state of her way.
sentences.i: When day came, the sultan fasted, and the old woman went off on her way.
sentences.n: إلى حال سبيلها, literally “to the state of her way,” is an idiom for going about one’s own business.

sentences.t: وَأَتَمَّ الْمَلِكُ صَوْمَ الْعَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الْحَادِي عَشَرَ فَتَحَ الْكُوزَ وَشَرِبَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-atamma al-maliku ṣawma al-ʿasharati ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-ḥādī ʿashara fataḥa al-kūza wa-sharibahu
sentences.l: And the king completed the fast of the ten days, and on the day the eleventh he opened the jug and drank it.
sentences.i: The king completed the fast of the first ten days, and on the eleventh day he opened the jug and drank from it.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدَ لَهُ فِي فُؤَادِهِ فِعْلًا جَمِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-wajada lahu fī fuʾādihi fiʿlan jamīlan
sentences.l: And he found for it in his heart a deed beautiful.
sentences.i: And he felt in his heart that it worked a pleasing effect.

sentences.t: وَفِى الْعَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ الثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ الشَّهْرِ جَاءَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَمَعَهَا حَلَاوَةٌ فِي وَرَقٍ أَخْضَرَ لَايُشْبِهُ وَرَقَ الشَّجَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-ʿasharati ayyāmin al-thāniyati mina al-shahri jāʾati al-ʿajūzu wa-maʿahā ḥalāwatun fī waraqin akhḍara lā yushbihu waraqa al-shajari
sentences.l: And in the ten days, the second, of the month, the old-woman came, and with her a sweetmeat in leaf green, not resembling the leaf of the tree.
sentences.i: In the second ten days of the month the old woman came with a sweetmeat wrapped in green leaves unlike the leaves of any tree.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتْ عَلَى وَالِدِكَ وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalat ʿalā wālidika wa-sallamat ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And she entered upon your father and greeted him.
sentences.i: She went in to your father and greeted him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا قَامَ لَهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا مَرْحَبًا بِالسَّيِّدَةِ الصَّالِحَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā qāma lahā wa-qāla lahā marḥaban bi-al-sayyidati al-ṣāliḥati
sentences.l: And when he saw her, he rose for her and said to her: Spaciousness to the lady, the righteous.
sentences.i: When he saw her he rose for her and said, “Welcome to the pious lady.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّ رِجَالَ الْغَيْبِ يُسَلِّمُونَ عَلَيْكَ لِأَنِّي أَخْبَرْتُهُمْ عَنْكَ فَفَرِحُوا بِكَ وَأَرْسَلُوا مَعِي هَذِهِ الْحَلَاوَةَ وَهِيَ مِنْ حَلَاوَةِ الْآخِرَةِ فَأَفْطِرْ عَلَيْهَا فِي آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ayyuhā al-maliku inna rijāla al-ghaybi yusallimūna ʿalayka li-annī akhbartuhum ʿanka fa-fariḥū bika wa-arsalū maʿī hādhihi al-ḥalāwata wa-hiya min ḥalāwati al-ākhirati fa-afṭir ʿalayhā fī ākhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: And she said to him: O king, indeed the men of the unseen greet you, because I informed-them about you, and they rejoiced in you and sent with me this sweetmeat, and it is from the sweetness of the hereafter, so break-your-fast on it at the end of the day.
sentences.i: She said to him: “O king, the Men of the Unseen send you their greetings, for I told them about you, and they rejoiced in you and sent this sweetmeat with me. It is from the sweets of the world to come; break your fast with it at the day’s end.”
sentences.n: رجال الغيب, “the men of the unseen,” are the hidden saints of Sufi belief, who are said to govern the world out of sight; the old woman uses them as her cover.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ وَالِدُكَ فَرَحًا زَائِدًا وَقَالَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لِي إِخْوَانًا مِنْ رِجَالِ الْغَيْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa wāliduka faraḥan zāʾidan wa-qāla al-ḥamdu li-llāhi alladhī jaʿala lī ikhwānan min rijāli al-ghaybi
sentences.l: And your father rejoiced a rejoicing excessive, and said: The praise is for God, who made for me brothers from the men of the unseen.
sentences.i: Your father was overjoyed, and said, “Praise be to God, who has given me brothers among the Men of the Unseen.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَكَرَ الْعَجُوزَ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَيْهَا وَأَكْرَمَهَا وَأَكْرَمَ الْجَوَارِيَ غَايَةَ الْإِكْرَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma shakara al-ʿajūza wa-qabbala yadayhā wa-akramahā wa-akrama al-jawāriya ghāyata al-ikrāmi
sentences.l: Then he thanked the old-woman and kissed her two hands and honoured her and honoured the slave-girls to the utmost of honouring.
sentences.i: Then he thanked the old woman, kissed her hands, and showed her and the girls every honour.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَتْ مُدَّةُ عِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا وَأَبُوكَ صَائِمٌ وَعِنْدَ رَأْسِ الْعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْعَجُوزُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma maḍat muddatu ʿishrīna yawman wa-abūka ṣāʾimun wa-ʿinda raʾsi al-ʿishrīna yawman aqbalat ʿalayhi al-ʿajūzu wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: Then a period of twenty days passed, and your father fasting, and at the head of the twenty days the old-woman came at him and said to him:
sentences.i: Then twenty days went by, with your father still fasting, and when the twenty days were at an end the old woman came to him and said:

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ اعْلَمْ أَنِّي أَخْبَرْتُ رِجَالَ الْغَيْبِ بِمَا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ مِنَ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَأَعْلَمْتُهُمْ بِأَنِّي تَرَكْتُ الْجَوَارِيَ عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku iʿlam annī akhbartu rijāla al-ghaybi bi-mā baynī wa-baynaka mina al-maḥabbati wa-aʿlamtuhum bi-annī taraktu al-jawāriya ʿindaka
sentences.l: O king, know that I informed the men of the unseen of what is between me and you of love, and I made them know that I left the slave-girls with you.
sentences.i: “O king, know that I told the Men of the Unseen of the love between you and me, and let them know that I had left the girls in your keeping.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحُوا حَيْثُ كَانَتِ الْجَوَارِي عِنْدَ مَلِكٍ مِثْلِكَ لِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا إِذَا رَأَوْهُنَّ يُبَالِغُونَ لَهُنَّ فِى الدُّعَاءِ الْمُسْتَجَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥū ḥaythu kānati al-jawārī ʿinda malikin mithlika li-annahum kānū idhā raʾawhunna yubālighūna lahunna fī al-duʿāʾi al-mustajābi
sentences.l: And they rejoiced since the slave-girls were with a king like you, because they used, when they saw them, to go to the limit for them in the prayer, the answered.
sentences.i: They were glad that the girls were with a king like you, for whenever they see them they pray for them without stint, and their prayer is answered.
sentences.n: كانوا إذا رأوهن يبالغون: kāna with a present-tense verb gives a habit, “whenever they saw them they would…”.

sentences.t: فَأُرِيدُأَنْ أَذْهَبَ بِهِنَّ إِلَى رِجَالِ الْغَيْبِ لِتَحْصُلَ نَفَحَاتُهُمْ لَهُنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-urīdu an adhhaba bihinna ilā rijāli al-ghaybi li-taḥṣula nafaḥātuhum lahunna
sentences.l: So I want that I go with them to the men of the unseen, that their breaths-of-grace may come about for them.
sentences.i: So I wish to take them to the Men of the Unseen, that their blessings may light upon them.”
sentences.n: نفحات (nafaḥāt, “breaths”) is the Sufi word for gusts of divine favour; the print runs فأريد and أن together.

sentences.t: وَرُبَّمَا أَنَّهُنَّ لَايَرْجِعْنَ إِلَيْكَ إِلَّا وَمَعَهُنَّ كَنْزٌ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْأَرْضِ حَتَّى أَنَّكَ بَعْدَ تَمَامِ صَوْمِكَ تَشْتَغِلُ بِكِسْوَتِهِنَّ وَتَسْتَعِينُ بِالْمَالِ الَّذِي يَأْ تِينَكَ بِهِ عَلَى أَغْرَاضِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-rubbamā annahunna lā yarjiʿna ilayka illā wa-maʿahunna kanzun min kunūzi al-arḍi ḥattā annaka baʿda tamāmi ṣawmika tashtaghilu bi-kiswatihinna wa-tastaʿīnu bi-al-māli alladhī yaʾ tīnaka bihi ʿalā aghrāḍika
sentences.l: And perhaps that they will not return to you except and with them a treasure of the treasures of the earth, until that you, after the completion of your fast, will busy yourself with their clothing and seek-help by the wealth which they-bring-you with it for your purposes.
sentences.i: “And perhaps they will return to you only with a treasure from the treasures of the earth, so that when your fast is complete you may busy yourself with clothing them, and use for your ends the wealth they bring you.”
sentences.n: The print splits يأتينك into يا تينك; the spacing is kept as set. Read it as one word, “they (the girls) bring you.” بِـ in بِالْمَالِ is the instrument (“by means of the wealth”); the به that follows takes it up again.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُكَ كَلَامَهَا شَكَرَهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ لَهَا لَوْلَا أَنِّي أَخْشَى مُخَالَفَتِي لَكِ مَارَضِيتُ بِالْكَنْزِ وَلَا غَيْرِهِ وَلَكِنْ مَتَى تَخْرُجِينَ بِهِنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduka kalāmahā shakarahā ʿalā dhālika wa-qāla lahā lawlā annī akhshā mukhālafatī laki mā raḍītu bi-al-kanzi wa-lā ghayrihi wa-lākin matā takhrujīna bihinna
sentences.l: And when your father heard her speech, he thanked her for that and said to her: Were it not that I fear my opposing of you, I would not have been pleased with the treasure, nor other-than-it; but when will you go out with them?
sentences.i: When your father heard what she said, he thanked her for it, and said, “But for my fear of going against you, I would not have been content with the treasure or with anything else. But when will you set out with them?”
sentences.n: مخالفتي لك, “my opposing you,” is an odd phrasing (one expects مخالفتك); it is read as it stands. رضي بـ takes بِـ: “be pleased with.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ فِى اللَّيْلَةِ السَّابِعَةِ وَالْعِشْرِينَ وَأَرْجِعُ بِهِنَّ إِلَيْكَ فِي رَأْسِ الشَّهْرِ وَتَكُونُ أَنْتَ قَدْأَوْفَيْتَ الصَّوْمَ وَحَصَلَ اسْتَبْرَأُوهُنَّ وَصِرْنَ لَكَ وَتَحْتَ أَمْرِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu fī al-laylati al-sābiʿati wa-al-ʿishrīna wa-arjiʿu bihinna ilayka fī raʾsi al-shahri wa-takūnu anta qad awfayta al-ṣawma wa-ḥaṣala istabraʾūhunna wa-ṣirna laka wa-taḥta amrika
sentences.l: And she said to him: On the night, the seventh and the twenty, and I will return with them to you at the head of the month, and you will be having fulfilled the fast, and it has come about that they cleared them, and they have become yours and under your command.
sentences.i: She said to him, “On the twenty-seventh night. I shall bring them back to you at the start of the month, when you will have completed your fast, and they will have been cleared, and the girls will be yours and under your command.
sentences.n: In استبرأوهن the print has a verb, “they cleared them”; the sense wants the noun استبراؤهن, “their clearing” (the waiting period that shows a slave-girl is not with child). The print is kept as it stands.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ كُلَّ جَارِيَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ ثَمَنُهَا أَعْظَمُ مِنْ مُلْكِكَ مَرَّاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-llāhi inna kulla jāriyatin minhunna thamanuhā aʿẓamu min mulkika marrātin
sentences.l: By God, indeed every slave-girl among them, her price is greater than your kingdom, times.
sentences.i: By God, the price of each one of them is many times greater than your kingdom.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا وَأَنَا أَعْرِفُ ذَلِكَ أَيَّتُهَا السَّيِّدَةُ الصَّالِحَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā wa-anā aʿrifu dhālika ayyatuhā al-sayyidatu al-ṣāliḥatu
sentences.l: And he said to her: And I know that, O lady, the righteous.
sentences.i: He said to her, “I know that, good lady.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَلَابُدَّأَنْ تُرْسِلَ مَعَهُنَّ مَنْ يَعِزُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَصْرِكَ حَتَّى يَجِدَ الْأُنْسَ وَيَلْتَمِسَ الْبَرَكَةَ مِنْ رِجَالِ الْغَيْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu baʿda dhālika wa-lā budda an tursila maʿahunna man yaʿizzu ʿalayka min qaṣrika ḥattā yajida al-unsa wa-yaltamisa al-barakata min rijāli al-ghaybi
sentences.l: And she said to him after that: And it is not avoidable that you send with them one who is dear upon you from your palace, so that he may find the familiarity and seek the blessing from the men of the unseen.
sentences.i: She said to him then, “And you must send with them someone dear to you from your palace, so that he too may find companionship and seek the blessing of the Men of the Unseen.”
sentences.n: ولابد أن, “and there is no avoiding that,” is written as one word in the print (ولابدان).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا عِنْدِي جَارِيَةٌ رُومِيَّةٌ اسْمُهَا صَفِيَّةُ وَرُزِقْتُ مِنْهَا بِوَلَدَيْنِ أُنْثَى وَذَكَرٍ وَلَكِنَّهُمَا فُقِدَا مِنْ مُنْذُ سِنِينَ فَخُذِيهَا مَعَهُنَّ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَحْصُلَ لَهَا الْبَرَكَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā ʿindī jāriyatun rūmiyyatun ismuhā ṣafiyyatu wa-ruziqtu minhā bi-waladayni unthā wa-dhakarin wa-lākinnahumā fuqidā min mundhu sinīna fa-khudhīhā maʿahunna li-ajli an taḥṣula lahā al-barakatu
sentences.l: And he said to her: I have a slave-girl, a Rūmī, her name Ṣafiyya, and I was provided by her with two children, a female and a male, but the two of them were lost from since years; so take her with them, for the sake that the blessing may come about for her.
sentences.i: He said to her, “I have a Rūmī slave-girl named Ṣafiyya, and I have two children by her, a girl and a boy, but they have been missing for years. Take her with them, so that she too may receive the blessing.”
sentences.n: The print has بوالدين (“with two parents”), a misprint for بولدين (“with two children”), corrected here. رُومِيَّة is a Rūmī, a Byzantine, so a Greek-speaking woman of the Christian Mediterranean. من منذ doubles the preposition (min, “from,” and mundhu, “since”); it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, with its rhyme on -āḥ, as in every night.
